article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors secured shareholder backing for its €3.91‑billion takeover of Iveco, with 87.81% of shares (238,157,212 shares) tendered, exceeding the 80% threshold and setting up a combined group with about €21 billion revenue and >590,000 vehicles.

The €3.91‑billion Iveco bid reached its final tender deadline on 26 Oct, with Tata confident of crossing the 80% acceptance level; activist Petrus Advisers challenged the valuation, while industry observers noted weak European demand, high electrification costs and emissions‑compliance pressures.

Tata Motors and Amazon announced a collaboration to deploy 3,000 electric trucks for Amazon’s logistics network in India over the next three years, with the first fleet flagged off by the Heavy Industries Minister.

Tata Motors completed the acquisition of Iveco, after nearly 88% of shares were tendered; the deal, valued at about $4.5 billion, combines >540,000 vehicles and >$25 billion revenue, and brings new board members from Tata to Iveco.

Settlement of the Iveco tender offer was finalized on 30 Oct, giving Tata Motors approximately 89.42% of Iveco’s share capital; the announcement detailed board composition changes and an advance of Iveco’s Q3 2026 results to 3 Nov.

key_points.text: Tata Motors obtained 87.81% shareholder acceptance for its €3.91‑billion takeover of Iveco, clearing the 80% threshold and moving towards settlement.
The acquisition creates a global commercial‑vehicle group with combined annual revenue of approximately €21 billion and sales of over 590,000 vehicles.
Tata Motors raised its offer price to €14.40 per share (a 2.1% increase from €14.10) as the final consideration.
Activist investor Petrus Advisers argued the offer undervalues Iveco, estimating a fair value of about €18 per share, roughly 25% above the bid.
Tata Motors completed the Iveco acquisition, holding about 89.42% of Iveco’s share capital after settlement, and announced board changes and forthcoming Q3 results.
The combined business now includes Iveco’s strong positions in Europe and Latin America and Tata’s presence in India and Africa, expanding geographic exposure (Europe 46%, India 32%).
Tata Motors and Amazon signed a partnership to deploy 3,000 electric trucks for Amazon’s logistics network in India over the next three years.

industry_context.text: European truckmakers are experiencing weak demand, high electrification spending, emissions‑compliance costs and rising competition, which could affect the merged entity’s performance.
India’s freight transportation demand is expected to grow with the economy, prompting emphasis on energy‑efficient commercial vehicle electrification.
